labels.label: bzprop:c3s4p10_contingent_conique
labels.notes: Left unmarked: no **`bzprop:c3s4p10...`** mark anywhere in lean-benzecri, and REPORT and docstring both disclose it as partial on OQ-169 (a), which is OPEN. prop10_contingent_conique_of_ne_interior has the same conclusion, verbatim, as Benzecri.prop10_contingent_conique (FacetteConique.lean:481). It swaps the hypothesis supportK F != univ for F != interior W. By supportK_ne_univ_iff the two are equivalent for any facette of a convex body, so the added hypothesis excludes exactly the interior facette. At that facette the printed statement fails (interior_facette_conique: int W is conical, has support S(n), and S(n)/S(n) is empty). Hypothesis by hypothesis: (1) facetteK_eq_interior needs only IsConvexPart W and a in int W. That is more general than the paper's convex body and not vacuous. Convexity is used, through convex_kPrime and combo_self_interior_mem_interior. (2) eq_interior_of_supportK_eq_univ needs IsConvexPart W, IsFacetteK W F and supportK F = univ. All three are needed and none is vacuous; the instance interior_simplexS_facette satisfies them. (3) isFacetteK_supportK_eq_univ_iff assumes IsCorpsConvexeS. The forward direction needs only IsConvexPart. The reverse direction needs int W nonempty, since otherwise F = int W = empty is not a facette, but it does not need compactness or strictness. So the hypothesis is slightly stronger than needed but matches the paper's setting. This is an observation, not a defect. (4) supportK_ne_univ_iff is the exact converse: not_congr of the two directions of the iff, with IsFacetteK W F needed for the forward direction. It carries the same convex-body hypothesis as (3). (5) The corollary's hypotheses are jointly satisfiable: prop10_of_ne_interior_instance gives the closed triangle simplexS 2, which is a convex body, with the vertex facette {s(e0)}, which is conical and is not int T. The finding that the printed statement fails at exactly one conical facette, int W, is correct as stated.

findings.what: isFacetteK_supportK_eq_univ_iff and supportK_ne_univ_iff assume IsCorpsConvexeS n W. What they use is IsConvexPart W together with (interior W).Nonempty; compactness and strictness are unused. This is not a faithfulness issue, because Prop. 10's W is a convex body. It is noted only because the dispatch asked whether any hypothesis is stronger than needed.
findings.fix: Optional: state both under IsConvexPart W and (interior W).Nonempty, and keep the convex-body forms as corollaries. No change is required.
